method_note: Desk audit. Primary texts were read through a fetch tool that summarises each page against a prompt, so section and line locators come from those summaries and should be spot-checked against the PDF before external citation. Ledger field names are the dotted paths of ledger/schema.py (cc-claim-ledger/0.1). Gap codes G1-G10 are defined in AB13_regulation_map.md. Nothing here is legal advice.

gap_codes.G1: plan binding: no hash or timestamp proving the analysis configuration and knowledge were fixed before the data were seen, and no deviations list
gap_codes.G2: question, estimand and context of use: no field states what causal question the graph serves or what it will be used for
gap_codes.G3: data lineage: data_sha256 identifies bytes, not source, version, extraction date, cleaning, linkage, missing-data handling or variable definitions
gap_codes.G4: human review: no record of who reviewed, accepted, overrode or rejected a claim, when, and why
gap_codes.G5: assumptions and sensitivity: identifying assumptions (sufficiency, faithfulness, acyclicity, alpha) and sensitivity runs are not typed records
gap_codes.G6: performance with intervals: calibration has a set id but no metric, interval, or proof the set is disjoint from the analysed data
gap_codes.G7: audit trail: one created_utc per run; no per-record timestamps, signatures, data-access log or retention statement
gap_codes.G8: multiplicity: no link between runs, so discarded runs, alternative data sources and exploratory analyses are invisible
gap_codes.G9: derived quantities: no adjustment set or downstream estimate is derived from the final graph and recorded
gap_codes.G10: tool lifecycle: no change log tying ledger format and engine versions across releases

rows.instrument: FDA draft guidance: Considerations for the Use of AI to Support Regulatory Decision-Making for Drug and Biological Products
rows.issuer: FDA (CDER, CBER, CDRH, CVM, OCE, OCP, OII)
rows.date: 2025-01 (docket FDA-2024-D-4689; still draft on FDA page as read 2026-10-12)
rows.requirement: Define the question of interest and the context of use (the model's role, what output is used for, what other evidence it is combined with); then rate model risk as model influence times decision consequence and scale credibility work to it.
rows.applies_to_causal_tool: conditional: only when the AI output produces information or data used to support a regulatory decision on safety, effectiveness or quality
rows.gap: G2: no question or context-of-use field; regime and direction_source show how much knowledge shaped the output but no influence/consequence rating is recorded
rows.label: read (primary)

rows.requirement: The credibility plan describes the model: inputs, outputs, architecture, features, parameters and the rationale for the modelling approach.
rows.gap: engine configuration (CI test, alpha, score, max conditioning size) is not a required field; licensed_by names the rule but not its parameters
rows.label: read (primary)

rows.requirement: Describe development and evaluation data: how collected, processed, stored and controlled, and whether fit for use; reliable data are accurate, complete and traceable.
rows.gap: G3: hashes prove which bytes were analysed, not where they came from or how they were processed
rows.label: read (primary)

rows.requirement: Track software version changes during training; name the sources of any pre-trained models; manage and report model changes over the life cycle.
rows.gap: G10 (minor): versions are pinned per run, but there is no change log across tool releases; model_id is a free string with no snapshot date
rows.label: read (primary)

rows.requirement: Give performance metrics with confidence intervals, estimate and interpret uncertainty of outputs, and consider repeatability or reproducibility studies.
rows.gap: G6: no calibration metric with interval; seed-to-seed repeatability is not recorded as a check the way order invariance is
rows.label: read (primary)

rows.requirement: Where a human is in the loop, evaluate the performance of the human-AI team, not the model alone.
rows.applies_to_causal_tool: conditional: applies to an analyst-plus-tool workflow
rows.gap: G4: person-supplied knowledge is recorded, but a human's decision on the output (accept, edit, reject a claim) is not
rows.label: read (primary)

rows.requirement: Document results of the plan and any deviations from it in a credibility assessment report, held for FDA on request or submitted.
rows.gap: G1: there is no plan object, so deviations cannot be stated against it
rows.label: read (primary)

rows.instrument: FDA draft guidance: Real-World Evidence: Considerations Regarding Non-Interventional Studies for Drug and Biological Products
rows.requirement: Finalise the protocol before the study is conducted and prespecify the statistical analysis plan.
rows.applies_to_causal_tool: conditional: when tool output enters a non-interventional study submitted to FDA
rows.gap: G1: nothing proves the engine config and knowledge set existed before the data hash was first computed
rows.label: read (primary)

rows.requirement: Include in the protocol a causal diagram (DAGs or SWIGs given as examples) showing the theorised causal relationships, and describe the approach to causal inference.
rows.applies_to_causal_tool: yes when used to build or check that diagram
rows.gap: partial: FDA's diagram is an a priori theory; the ledger has no flag separating a prespecified hypothesised graph (as knowledge) from the discovered one, and no export of the final graph as a protocol figure
rows.label: read (primary)

rows.requirement: The analysis plan says how confounding will be handled, including an assessment of unmeasured confounding and overadjustment on intermediates, and describes planned sensitivity analyses (what is varied and why).
rows.gap: G5 and G9: causal sufficiency is not recorded as an assumption; bootstrap is the only typed perturbation; no adjustment set or mediator list is derived from the final graph
rows.label: read (primary)

rows.instrument: FDA guidance: Real-World Data: Assessing EHR and Medical Claims Data To Support Regulatory Decision-Making
rows.requirement: Give conceptual and operational (code-based) definitions for population, exposure, outcome and covariates, with computable phenotypes in machine-processable form; disclose unmeasured or imperfectly measured confounders and justify proxies; reliability includes traceability (known provenance, e.g. an audit trail).
rows.locator: III; IV.B.4; IV.D.1; V.E.1, V.E.3; I (fn 11)
rows.applies_to_causal_tool: yes: each node of a causal graph is such a variable
rows.gap: G3: a variable has a name and content hash but no definition, code-list hash or proxy flag; provenance stops at the hash
rows.label: read (primary)

rows.requirement: Describe reasons for missing data, state the missingness assumptions and run sensitivity analyses on them.
rows.applies_to_causal_tool: yes: CI tests and scores depend on how missing rows were handled
rows.gap: G3 and G5: no record of deletion or imputation, nor of the missingness assumption the tests relied on
rows.label: read (primary)

rows.instrument: FDA guidance: Considerations for the Use of RWD and RWE to Support Regulatory Decision-Making for Drug and Biological Products
rows.requirement: Keep audit trails from RWD extraction to dataset retention that track user access, data changes, protocol changes and analyses; electronic systems meet 21 CFR part 11.
rows.applies_to_causal_tool: conditional: when tool runs are analyses in a submitted study
rows.gap: G7: the hash gives integrity but not authenticity; there is no signature, access log or per-record timestamp
rows.label: read (primary)

rows.requirement: Document data, code and algorithms well enough for FDA to replicate the analysis.
rows.gap: mostly met: engine, version, wheel hash, seed and data hash pin a rerun; missing are the engine configuration (see FDA AI row 2) and the preprocessing code hash (G3)
rows.label: read (primary)

rows.requirement: Document the data sources evaluated and why each was chosen or excluded; label analyses outside the SAP as exploratory; identify and document protocol and SAP deviations; date-stamp revisions.
rows.gap: G1 and G8: no plan, no deviations, no exploratory flag, no links to other runs on other data
rows.label: read (primary)

rows.instrument: FDA draft guidance: Considerations for the Design and Conduct of Externally Controlled Trials
rows.requirement: Submit the SAP before enrolment; do not make design decisions while viewing external-control outcomes; date and justify any SAP change.
rows.gap: G1: supplier.shown records what a knowledge supplier saw (analogous to blinding), but there is no plan hash and no proof of ordering
rows.label: read (primary)

rows.requirement: Describe every data source accessed while designing the control arm, including feasibility and exploratory analyses; generate audit trails of access to and analyses of those sources; make assumptions explicit and test them with sensitivity and bias analyses.
rows.label: read (primary)

rows.instrument: FDA guidance: Use of Real-World Evidence to Support Regulatory Decision-Making for Medical Devices
rows.requirement: Identify the first instance of the data, keep a data audit trail and retain transformations to a common data model; name RWD sources, versions and extraction dates.
rows.gap: G3
rows.label: read (primary)

rows.requirement: Protocol includes causal diagrams; protocol and analysis plan are finalised before outcome data are reviewed; revisions are dated, time-stamped and justified; key design decisions and rationale documented.
rows.gap: G1: graph and per-edge rationale are present; the time-stamped plan is not
rows.label: read (primary)

rows.instrument: Guiding Principles of Good AI Practice in Drug Development
rows.requirement: Record data origin, processing steps and the reasons for analytical choices so every step can be traced and verified (principle 6); evaluate the whole system including human interaction (principle 8).
rows.applies_to_causal_tool: yes for AI used in drug development evidence
rows.gap: reasons for analytical choices are met at claim level (V2 closure); G3 for processing steps; G4 for human interaction
rows.label: read (primary)

rows.requirement: Give plain-language information on purpose, performance, limitations, underlying data, updates and how to understand outputs.
rows.gap: the rendered human-readable report is promised in DESIGN.md but not specified; purpose field missing (G2)
rows.label: read (primary)

rows.instrument: EMA Reflection paper on the use of AI in the medicinal product lifecycle (EMA/CHMP/CVMP/83833/2023)
rows.requirement: Document data sources, acquisition and every processing step in a detailed and fully traceable way, in line with GxP; keep development logs that allow secondary assessment.
rows.applies_to_causal_tool: conditional: AI used in evidence for EU medicines regulation
rows.gap: G3 for processing before the hash; analysis steps after the hash are met
rows.label: read (primary)

rows.requirement: In pivotal trials, freeze and record the preprocessing pipeline and all models in the SAP before database lock; incremental learning is not accepted there.
rows.gap: G1: frozen components are identified, but nothing proves they were frozen before database lock
rows.label: read (primary)

rows.requirement: Prefer transparent models; black boxes need justification; explainability methods encouraged.
rows.gap: none: each mark is explained by a named rule and the tests it fired on
rows.label: read (primary)

rows.requirement: Generative language models can give plausible but wrong output, so their output needs close human supervision and quality review.
rows.gap: G4: LLM statements are isolated and cannot add edges (V3), but a human's review of them is not recorded
rows.label: read (primary)

rows.instrument: CHMP Qualification opinion for Prognostic Covariate Adjustment (PROCOVA), Unlearn.AI
rows.requirement: The prognostic score is prespecified before unblinding, defined independently of the study data, and its weights are not adjusted to the trial.
rows.applies_to_causal_tool: precedent, not a requirement: shows the conditions under which EMA qualified an ML component
rows.gap: G1: binding times in DESIGN.md say knowledge is fixed before resolution, but the record cannot prove it was fixed before the data were seen
rows.label: read (primary)

rows.requirement: Type I error control, unbiasedness and interval coverage do not depend on the prognostic model's performance; only efficiency does (asymptotically, under stated assumptions).
rows.applies_to_causal_tool: precedent: the regulator accepted ML because the inferential guarantee is independent of ML quality
rows.gap: partial: V3 and V8 give the analogous floor for the skeleton (knowledge never connects); orientations from knowledge carry no error guarantee, and the floor's own finite-sample error is not stated
rows.label: read (primary)

rows.requirement: Validate on data independent of both training and study data to avoid optimistic estimates; run sensitivity analyses on the assumed correlation.
rows.gap: G6: calibration_set is an id, not a data hash, so disjointness from the analysed data cannot be checked
rows.label: read (primary)

rows.instrument: ICH E9(R1) Addendum on estimands and sensitivity analysis in clinical trials
rows.requirement: Define the estimand (treatment, population, variable, intercurrent-event handling, population-level summary) in the protocol before the trial; the principles also apply to observational studies.
rows.applies_to_causal_tool: conditional: a discovery graph is upstream of an estimand, not an estimand; applies when the graph selects the adjustment set for one
rows.gap: G2 and G9
rows.label: read (primary)

rows.requirement: State the key assumptions of the main estimator explicitly; plan sensitivity analyses in advance; report main, sensitivity and supplementary results, labelling each as prespecified, introduced while blinded, or post hoc.
rows.applies_to_causal_tool: yes by analogy: discovery output rests on identifying assumptions
rows.gap: G5 and G1: invariants I1-I7 are properties of the tool, not the world assumptions (sufficiency, faithfulness, acyclicity, alpha) the claims rest on; no prespecified/post hoc label on a run
rows.label: read (primary)

rows.instrument: EU AI Act, Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, Art. 6, Art. 2 and Annex III
rows.date: 2024-06-13; Annex III duties apply from 2027-12-02 and Annex I from 2028-08-02 after the Digital Omnibus (Council final approval 2026-06-29)
rows.requirement: A system is high-risk if it is a safety component of an Annex I product needing third-party assessment, or is used in an Annex III area (e.g. credit scoring, life/health insurance pricing, employment, essential benefits); an Annex III system may escape via the narrow-task or preparatory-task derogation, unless it profiles people, and the provider must document that assessment. AI used solely for scientific research, and pre-market R&D, are outside the Act.
rows.applies_to_causal_tool: conditional: a causal-analysis tool is not high-risk as such; it becomes high-risk when deployed for an Annex III purpose (e.g. inside credit or insurance pricing) or as part of a regulated medical device; academic research use is excluded
rows.gap: G2: no intended-purpose field from which the classification could be read
rows.label: read (primary)

rows.instrument: EU AI Act Art. 12 and Art. 19 (record-keeping, log retention)
rows.requirement: High-risk systems log events automatically over their lifetime, giving traceability for risk situations, post-market monitoring and operational monitoring; providers keep logs they control for at least six months.
rows.gap: G7: one ledger per run is an event log for that run, but there is no cross-run log, per-event timestamp or retention statement
rows.label: read (primary)

rows.instrument: EU AI Act Art. 13 (transparency to deployers)
rows.requirement: Instructions state intended purpose, accuracy levels and the metrics used, factors affecting them, and specifications of input and training/validation data.
rows.gap: G6 and G2
rows.label: read (primary)

rows.instrument: EU AI Act Art. 13 (transparency to deployers)
rows.requirement: Disclose foreseeable circumstances that create risk, features that help explain outputs, information for interpreting outputs, and mechanisms for collecting and interpreting logs.
rows.gap: none in the format; verify.py is the log-interpretation mechanism
rows.label: read (primary)

rows.requirement: Overseers must be able to understand capabilities and limits, stay aware of automation bias, interpret output correctly, and decide to disregard, override or reverse an output.
rows.gap: G4: data_only_relation shows what the data alone support (an aid against automation bias), but a human override of a claim has no record type; overrides covers only knowledge vs. intervention
rows.label: read (primary)

rows.date: 2024-06-13 (Art. 10(1) amended by Digital Omnibus per Service Desk)
rows.requirement: Training, validation and test data practices cover design choices, data origin and collection, preparation, the assumptions about what data represent, bias examination and data gaps.
rows.applies_to_causal_tool: conditional: high-risk and only where the system trains models (calibration fit counts)
rows.gap: G3 and G5
rows.label: read (primary)

rows.instrument: EU AI Act Art. 17 (quality management system)
rows.date: 2024-06-13 (Service Desk notes Omnibus amendments not yet shown)
rows.requirement: Providers keep a documented QMS including testing and validation procedures, data management across the data lifecycle, and record-keeping of relevant documentation.
rows.applies_to_causal_tool: conditional: provider of a high-risk system
rows.gap: mostly organisational and outside the record format; the ledger can be the per-run evidence a QMS points to
rows.label: read (primary)

rows.instrument: EU AI Act Annex IV (technical documentation)
rows.requirement: Document version and relation to earlier versions, design choices with rationale and assumptions, third-party pre-trained models used, datasheets on data origin and preparation, lifecycle changes, and validation and test logs that are dated and signed.
rows.gap: G7: test results exist but are unsigned; G5 assumptions; G3 datasheets; G10 change log
rows.label: read (primary)

rows.instrument: SR 26-2, Revised Guidance on Model Risk Management (supersedes SR 11-7 and SR 21-8)
rows.requirement: A model is a quantitative method applying statistical or economic theory to turn inputs into estimates; generative and agentic AI are outside this guidance; it is most relevant to banking organisations over $30bn in assets and states no prescriptive requirements.
rows.applies_to_causal_tool: conditional: a deterministic discovery engine used in a covered bank's decisions is a model; the LLM that supplies knowledge falls outside SR 26-2 and is left to the firm's own controls
rows.gap: none for scoping: the ledger already separates the in-scope model (engines) from out-of-scope generative input (supplier type model)
rows.label: read (primary)

rows.requirement: Document design choices, assumptions, judgements and data selection; effective challenge by objective, competent people with standing; ongoing monitoring and outcomes analysis; for vendor models, understand conceptual soundness and performance even when code is proprietary.
rows.gap: G5 assumptions; G4 the challenger's findings have no record; no link from claims to later observed intervention outcomes. Met: verify.py checks claims without code or data, which suits a validator facing a vendor tool
rows.label: read (primary)

rows.instrument: SR 11-7, Guidance on Model Risk Management (superseded by SR 26-2)
rows.date: 2011-04-04 (superseded 2026-04-17; the SR 11-7 page itself shows no superseded notice)
rows.requirement: Documentation detailed enough that parties unfamiliar with a model understand its operation, limits and key assumptions; validation covers conceptual soundness, ongoing monitoring and outcomes analysis.
rows.applies_to_causal_tool: historical: cite SR 26-2 for current US bank practice
rows.gap: G5 assumptions
rows.label: read (primary)

rows.instrument: TARGET Statement: transparent reporting of observational studies emulating a target trial
rows.requirement: List the assumptions needed to identify each causal estimand and the variables they involve; justify the baseline confounders chosen and say how they were measured.
rows.applies_to_causal_tool: yes when the graph is used to choose confounders
rows.gap: G5 and G9: confounder choice would follow from the graph, but the derived adjustment set and its assumptions are not recorded
rows.label: read (primary)

rows.requirement: Describe sensitivity analyses, their rationale and the biases they target, and report all their results; describe models and software; report availability of data, code and materials, and registration.
rows.gap: G5 sensitivity; G1 registration
rows.label: read (primary)

rows.requirement: Define every outcome, exposure, confounder and effect modifier and give data source and measurement for each; describe methods for confounding, missing data and sensitivity analyses; report which confounders were adjusted for and why.
rows.applies_to_causal_tool: yes when results are published as an observational study
rows.gap: G3 definitions; G9 adjustment set and its reason
rows.label: read (primary)

rows.requirement: Give complete code lists and algorithms for exposures, outcomes and confounders; describe data cleaning and record linkage and its quality; say how readers can obtain protocol, raw data and programming code.
rows.gap: G3
rows.label: read (primary)

rows.instrument: Tennant et al., Use of DAGs to identify confounders in applied health research: review and recommendations (IJE 2021)
rows.issuer: Tennant et al., Int J Epidemiol 50(2)
rows.requirement: Make every DAG available; assume arcs exist by default and justify each omitted arc with theory or evidence (only 6% of 144 DAG papers cited sources for arcs; none tested DAG-data consistency).
rows.gap: none: each absent pair is a claim citing the separating test; this is the strongest single fit in the map
rows.label: read (primary)

rows.requirement: State the focal relationship and estimand; state the DAG-implied adjustment set for each estimand and report its estimate even if not the main result; justify alternative sets.
rows.gap: G2 and G9
rows.label: read (primary)

rows.instrument: Ellison and Rhoma, DAGs as conceptual and analytical tools in applied and theoretical epidemiology (MBE 2025;22(6):1280-1306)
rows.requirement: Report the DAG's purpose and the reasoning for its arcs (theoretical, speculative or temporal); report unmeasured variables and temporal uncertainty; use machine-readable notation; compare results across plausible alternative DAGs. A narrative review, not a consensus checklist.
rows.gap: G5 alternative-DAG sensitivity; machine-readable export is planned (DESIGN.md section 5) but not built
rows.label: read (primary)

rows.instrument: ROBINS-E: risk of bias in non-randomized follow-up studies of exposure effects (Environment International, Apr 2024)
rows.requirement: Before rating bias, specify the result being assessed and the causal effect it estimates; then judge seven bias domains (confounding first among them) and the likely direction of bias.
rows.applies_to_causal_tool: conditional: an appraisal tool for studies a ledger might support, not a reporting duty
rows.gap: G2 and G5
rows.label: second-hand

rows.requirement: Format venue: Entity, Activity, Agent with wasGeneratedBy, used, wasDerivedFrom, wasAttributedTo, wasAssociatedWith; qualified terms (qualifiedDerivation, Plan, hadPlan); no notion of rules or confidence.
rows.applies_to_causal_tool: yes as a serialisation target, not a requirement
rows.gap: licensed_by maps naturally to prov:Plan via hadPlan; confidence and direction_source need an extension vocabulary; prov_export.py not written
rows.label: read (primary)

venues.venue: W3C AI Computed Provenance Community Group
venues.what could be proposed: A causal-claim profile: the PROV-O mapping in DESIGN.md section 4, plus the claim record (relation, direction_source, licensed_by as prov:Plan, data_only_relation, confidence) and the verifier checks V1-V8 as a conformance test, contributed as a use case and draft section of the group's reference specification
venues.fit: best: scope is provenance for AI-assisted science on the principle that a computed result differs from an asserted one; deliverables are a reference spec plus a conformance suite; free, no W3C membership, royalty-free report. Risks: proposed 2026-08-11, 14 participants, chair unsettled, no drafts seen, page does not mention PROV-O

venues.venue: Any new W3C Community Group (self-proposed, e.g. 'Causal Claims CG')
venues.what could be proposed: A Community Group Report defining the ledger as a PROV-O profile
venues.fit: fallback: free, short scope statement and a minimum number of supporters; Community Groups do not make W3C standards, only reports

venues.venue: OHDSI workgroups (HADES, Evidence Network, Generative AI and Analytics, Methods Research)
venues.what could be proposed: A ledger output from an OHDSI-style causal pipeline over OMOP CDM data, with lineage fields filled from CDM and phenotype metadata
venues.fit: good for RWE adoption and lineage (G3), but no workgroup is named for causal inference or discovery, and the Evidence Network 2025 OKRs say nothing about result schemas or provenance

venues.venue: Pistoia Alliance (Large Language Models in Life Sciences project; FAIR Implementation)
venues.what could be proposed: LLM-supplied knowledge records (supplier, prompt hash, shown) as an evaluation dimension in the Phase 2 benchmark
venues.fit: weak to moderate: industry reach, but the project page mentions no provenance, audit or causal reasoning, and Phase 2 is seeking sponsorship

venues.venue: ISO/IEC JTC 1/SC 42 (ISO/IEC 42001:2023 AI management system; ISO/IEC 5338:2023 AI lifecycle processes)
venues.what could be proposed: Nothing directly; the ledger could be cited as per-run evidence inside a 42001 management system or a 5338 lifecycle
venues.fit: poor as a venue for a student team: participation runs through national bodies; full texts are paywalled and were not read

venues.venue: IEEE Standards Association (IEEE 7001-2021 Transparency of Autonomous Systems; new PAR)
venues.what could be proposed: A PAR for a causal-claim record, or a mapping to 7001 transparency levels
venues.fit: poor: 7001 is published and targets autonomous systems; a new PAR needs a sponsor and working group; full text not read

venues.what could be proposed: A TARGET or STROBE extension item for machine-discovered or LLM-assisted causal diagrams (report per-edge source and data-only graph)
venues.fit: moderate, long-term: no formal consensus DAG reporting guideline was found, so the slot is open, but extensions need a Delphi process
